answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only when backed by a scarce, slashable deposit: each new identity must lock tokens, and its actions are limited by the deposit’s size. If an agent cheats or repeatedly breaks commitments, peers can submit evidence to trigger slashing, so splitting into many identities does not multiply influence for free. The river of newcomers may reach the harbor, but each must pay the same toll; a forge of fake accounts therefore ties up real capital and risks losing it.
